name: Dry Scalp
description: Hair with a dry scalp is characterized by lack of moisture, often leading to flakiness and discomfort. The scalp may also produce excess oil as a compensatory mechanism.
hair_texture: Thinner, more fragile texture that can appear dull and lifeless.
porosity: High porosity, where the cuticle layer is lifted or damaged, allowing for easy entry of products but also rapid loss of moisture.
characteristics: Dryness leading to breakage and brittleness
Visible dry patches on the hair shaft
common_problems: Increased susceptibility to damage from heat styling tools
Difficulty in holding hairstyles due to lack of moisture
recommended_ingredients: Oleic acid and other fatty acids
Intensive moisturizers such as shea butter, cocoa butter
ingredients_to_avoid: Parabens and other preservatives that can be drying
recommended_product_categories: Conditioners with a focus on hydration
washing_frequency: No more than twice a week, depending on oil production and scalp health.
oil_recommendation: Use of light-to-medium weight oils that can penetrate the scalp without leaving residue, such as jojoba or argan oil.

morning_routine.purpose: To lock in moisture and provide immediate hydration.

night_routine.action: Use an overnight oil treatment or deep conditioner
night_routine.purpose: To deeply moisturize the scalp and hair during sleep, allowing for better absorption.

weekly_care: Perform a deep conditioning treatment at least once a week to replenish moisture.
deep_conditioning_frequency: Once a week or as needed based on scalp condition.
heat_styling_recommendation: Limit heat styling and use protective styles whenever possible. If using heat, ensure the hair is well-conditioned beforehand.
lifestyle_tips: Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water
Use a wide-tooth comb to minimize breakage during detangling
foods_for_healthy_hair: Avocados and nuts (rich in healthy fats)
Fatty fish like salmon (for omega-3 fatty acids)
common_mistakes: Over-washing the hair, which can strip natural oils
Using harsh chemical treatments that further dry out the scalp
dont: Rough handling of hair when wet or dry

seasonal_care.summer: Focus on keeping the scalp cool and preventing excess oil production, use lightweight oils.
seasonal_care.winter: Intensify hydration routines to combat dry air and cold weather, apply extra moisturizing products.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Be cautious of increased humidity which can lead to more oiliness, but still ensure regular deep conditioning.

expert_tips: Regular scalp massages can help stimulate blood circulation and promote natural oils production.
Consider using a humidifier in dry environments to prevent hair from drying out too much.
